en: to confuse; to throw into disorder; to bewilder

examples.en: The sudden news threw people into confusion.
That rumor is throwing the village into disorder.
Did you do it on purpose to confuse me?
If you keep changing what you say, you confuse the students.
Please do not do things that cause confusion.

examples.ko: 새 규칙이 손님들을 혼란시킨 것 같아요.
examples.en: It seems the new rule confused the customers.

explain: '혼란시키다'는 누가 일부러든 아니든 다른 사람을 헷갈리게 하고 질서를 흐트러뜨릴 때 써요. 내가 헷갈릴 때는 '혼란스럽다'가 훨씬 자연스러워요. 일상에서는 '헷갈리게 하다'를 더 많이 말해요.

phrases.en: Please don't confuse me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대에게 헷갈리게 하지 말라고 부탁할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this to ask someone not to confuse you.

phrases.example: 말을 자꾸 바꾸면 사람들을 헷갈리게 해요.
phrases.en: If you keep changing what you say, you confuse people.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서는 '혼란시키다'보다 이 말을 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily speech, this is more common than '혼란시키다'.

phrases.en: The new rule caused confusion for the students.
phrases.nuance_ko: '에게'를 써서 누구에게 혼란을 주는지 말할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: You can use '에게' to say who is being confused.

explain_en: Causes confusion in people or situations; transitive, written. '혼란시키다' is used when something, on purpose or not, makes others confused and upsets order. When I am the confused one, '혼란스럽다' is much more natural. In daily talk, '헷갈리게 하다' is more common.

t90.ax: Did you do it on purpose to confuse me?

examples.en: I put a protective film over my phone screen.
Why are you trying to pin the blame on me?

examples.ko: 오래된 소파에 새 천을 덧씌워서 쓰고 있어요.
examples.en: I put a new cover over the old sofa and keep using it.

examples.ko: 친구가 제 그림 위에 투명 필름을 덧씌웠어요.
examples.en: My friend laid a clear film over my drawing.

examples.ko: 그 사람에게 나쁜 이미지를 덧씌우지 마세요.
examples.en: Please don't stick a bad image on that person.

examples.ko: 이미 끝난 일에 새 누명을 덧씌우면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You can't pin a new false charge on something that is already over.

explain: 물건 위에 한 겹 더 씌울 때도 쓰지만, 실제로는 '누명을 덧씌우다', '이미지를 덧씌우다'처럼 남에게 책임이나 나쁜 평가를 얹을 때 자주 들려요. 피동은 '덧씌워지다'예요.

phrases.example: 그 사람에게 누명을 덧씌우면 안 돼요.
phrases.en: You must not put a false accusation on that person.
phrases.nuance_ko: 남에게 억울한 죄를 얹는다는 뜻으로 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for putting a false charge on someone.

phrases.example: 뉴스가 그 가수에게 나쁜 이미지를 덧씌웠어요.
phrases.en: The news put a bad image on that singer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 원래 모습과 다른 평가를 얹을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when placing a judgment on someone that differs from reality.

phrases.en: A false accusation was laid on him.
phrases.nuance_ko: 피동형으로, 남이 얹은 누명이나 평가를 떠안게 되었다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The passive form: ending up saddled with an accusation or judgment placed by others.

explain_en: It can mean putting one more layer over something, but in real talk it often means pinning blame or a label on someone, as in '누명을 덧씌우다' or '이미지를 덧씌우다'. The passive form is '덧씌워지다'.

examples.en: They drew water up from the well with a pulley.

examples.ko: 도르래를 쓰면 무거운 짐도 쉽게 들 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you use a pulley, you can lift even heavy loads easily.
We did a pulley experiment in science class.
The pulley is rusty, so it makes a strange noise.

examples.ko: 공사장에서는 도르래에 줄을 걸어 벽돌을 올려요.
examples.en: At the construction site, they hang a rope on a pulley to raise bricks.

examples.ko: 이 커튼은 도르래 줄을 당기면 열려요.
examples.en: This curtain opens when you pull the pulley cord.

explain: 과학 시간에 많이 나오는 말이고, 일상에서는 우물, 공사장, 블라인드 같은 이야기에서 만나요. 보통 '도르래를 달다', '도르래를 쓰다'처럼 말해요.

phrases.en: We installed a pulley above the well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 도르래를 설치하는 동작을 말할 때 쓰는 가장 기본적인 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic pairing for setting up a pulley.

phrases.en: The workers hauled up the load with a pulley.
phrases.nuance_ko: 도르래를 이용해 무거운 것을 위로 올린다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means lifting something heavy by using a pulley.
phrases.en_equiv: to haul up with a pulley

phrases.en: We learned the principle of the pulley in science class.
phrases.nuance_ko: 수업이나 설명에서 도르래가 어떻게 작동하는지 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in lessons or explanations about how a pulley works.

explain_en: It comes up in science class, and in daily life in talk about wells, construction sites and blinds. People usually say '도르래를 달다' (to attach a pulley) or '도르래를 쓰다' (to use a pulley).

examples.en: I hung a mobile above the baby's crib.
The mobile is turning slowly in the wind.
My friend sent a mobile as a baby gift.

examples.ko: 저는 종이로 별 모양 모빌을 만들었어요.
examples.en: I made a star-shaped mobile out of paper.
The baby smiles whenever he sees the mobile.

examples.ko: 카페 천장에 예쁜 모빌이 걸려 있어요.
examples.en: A pretty mobile hangs from the cafe ceiling.

explain: 천장에 매달아 바람이나 손길에 흔들리게 하는 장식이에요. 아기 방 장식으로 가장 많이 써요. 휴대전화 쪽 말인 '모바일'과 헷갈리지 마세요.

phrases.en: I made a star-shaped mobile out of paper.
phrases.nuance_ko: 직접 손으로 만들 때 쓰고, 아이와 함께 하는 만들기에 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for making one by hand, often a craft with children.

phrases.en: When I opened the window, the mobile swayed gently.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바람이 불어서 움직이는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes it moving in the wind.

phrases.example: 친구가 출산 선물로 아기 모빌을 줬어요.
phrases.en: My friend gave me a baby mobile as a birth gift.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아기 침대 위에 다는 종류를 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the kind hung over a baby's crib.

explain_en: 모빌 is a decoration hung from the ceiling that sways in a breeze. It is most often a baby-room item. Don't mix it up with 모바일, the word for mobile phone or mobile use.

examples.ko: 열을 가하면 금속을 다른 모양으로 변형할 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you apply heat, you can reshape metal into another form.

examples.ko: 작가가 옛날이야기를 변형해서 새 소설을 썼어요.
examples.en: The author adapted an old tale and wrote a new novel.
The chef modified the traditional recipe a little.
A version that alters the original song is popular.
You must not change the rules however you like.

examples.ko: 그 디자이너는 같은 무늬를 계속 변형해요.
examples.en: That designer keeps modifying the same pattern.

explain: '변형하다'는 원래 모양이나 내용을 알아볼 수 있게 바꾸는 거예요. '바꾸다'는 아예 다른 것으로 바꿔도 쓰지만, '변형하다'는 원래 것이 남아 있어요. 바뀐 결과를 말할 때는 '변형되다'를 써요.

phrases.en: I changed the shape of the clay to make an animal.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건의 모양을 바꿀 때 쓰는 가장 기본적인 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic pairing for changing an object's shape.

phrases.en: I used the recipe with a few changes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 원래 것을 조금 바꿔서 사용할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you slightly alter something original and then use it.

phrases.en: Please don't modify the product on your own.
phrases.nuance_ko: 원래 모양이나 내용을 바꾸지 말라고 부탁하거나 안내할 때 쓰는 존댓말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite request or notice not to change the original form or content.

explain_en: 변형하다 means changing the original shape or content while it can still be recognized. 바꾸다 can be used even for swapping in something entirely different, but with 변형하다 the original remains. To describe the result of the change, use 변형되다.

examples.en: In a hanok, a foundation stone is placed under each pillar.

examples.ko: 튼튼한 주춧돌 위에 집을 지어야 안전해요.
examples.en: A house is safe only when built on a solid foundation stone.

examples.ko: 이 경험이 제 성공의 주춧돌이 되었어요.
examples.en: This experience became the foundation of my success.
My parents are the cornerstone of our family.

examples.ko: 오래된 주춧돌만 남아 있는 절터에 갔어요.
examples.en: I visited a temple site where only the old foundation stones remain.
I think studying the basics is the foundation of skill.

explain: 기둥 밑에 받쳐 놓는 돌인데, 비유로 '무엇의 바탕이 되는 것'이라는 뜻으로도 많이 써요. 한자어 '초석'과 뜻이 같고 글에서 조금 더 딱딱하게 들려요. 사람이나 경험이 바탕이 될 때 '~의 주춧돌이 되다'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 선생님께서 제 인생의 주춧돌을 놓아 주셨어요.
phrases.en: My teacher laid the foundation of my life.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실제 돌이 아니라 앞으로 일이 잘되도록 기초를 마련한다는 비유로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It is figurative rather than literal, meaning to prepare the groundwork so that later things go well.

explain_en: Literal stone under a pillar of a building; also figurative. It is the stone set beneath a pillar, and it is also widely used figuratively for the base of something. The Sino-Korean '초석' means the same and sounds a bit stiffer in writing. You say '~의 주춧돌이 되다' when a person or experience becomes the basis of something.

t90.ax: My parents are the cornerstone of our family.

examples.ko: 지렛대를 쓰면 무거운 돌도 움직일 수 있어요.
examples.en: With a lever, you can move even a heavy stone.
We learned the principle of the lever in science class.

examples.ko: 이 사업을 성공의 지렛대로 삼고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to use this business as a lever for success.

examples.ko: 지렛대 끝을 아래로 누르니까 돌이 올라왔어요.
examples.en: When I pushed the end of the lever down, the stone came up.
The longer the lever is, the less force you need.

examples.ko: 아이는 막대기를 지렛대 삼아 바위를 밀어 봤어요.
examples.en: The child used a stick as a lever and tried pushing the rock.

explain: 실제 도구뿐 아니라 '무언가를 이루기 위한 발판'이라는 비유로도 많이 써요. 뉴스나 경제 이야기에서 '성장의 지렛대'처럼 자주 나와요.

phrases.example: 이번 성공을 지렛대 삼아 해외로 나갈 거예요.
phrases.en: use as leverage; use as a stepping stone
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 결과나 상황을 이용해서 다음 목표로 나아간다는 뜻이에요. 사업이나 뉴스에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means using a result or situation to move toward the next goal. It is common in business and news.
phrases.en_equiv: use X as a stepping stone

explain_en: Besides the real tool, it is often used figuratively for something that helps you achieve a goal. In news and economic talk it appears often, as in '성장의 지렛대' (a lever for growth).

examples.ko: 다리 교각에 배가 부딪혔다는 뉴스를 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw news that a ship hit a bridge pier.
Many people fish under the bridge piers.
The newly built bridge pier looks sturdy.
The bridge piers were submerged because of the flood.

examples.ko: 이 다리는 교각이 열 개나 있어요.
examples.en: This bridge has as many as ten piers.
The river flows fast between the bridge piers.

explain: '다리'가 전체를 말한다면 '교각'은 강이나 땅에 서서 다리를 받치는 기둥 부분만 말해요. 일상 대화보다 뉴스나 공사, 사고 이야기에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: They built a bridge pier in the middle of the river.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다리를 만들 때 기둥을 세우는 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to putting up supporting columns when building a bridge.

phrases.en: The bridge pier collapsed in the flood.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 사고를 말할 때 자주 나오는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A phrase often seen in news reports about accidents.

phrases.en: The road is blocked because of the bridge pier construction.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다리 기둥을 만들거나 고치는 공사를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Construction work to build or repair bridge piers.

explain_en: Support column of a bridge, engineering term. While '다리' means the whole bridge, '교각' refers only to the pillars standing in the river or ground that hold it up. It appears more in news, construction and accident reports than in daily talk.

examples.ko: 이 약은 신경을 마비시키는 성분이 들어 있어요.
examples.en: This medicine contains an ingredient that numbs the nerves.
The heavy snow brought the city's traffic to a standstill.

examples.ko: 큰 홍수가 마을 전체를 마비시킬 정도였어요.
examples.en: The big flood was enough to bring the whole town to a standstill.

examples.ko: 독이 몸을 마비시켜서 움직일 수 없었어요.
examples.en: The poison paralyzed the body, so I couldn't move.

examples.ko: 두려움이 사람을 마비시켜 버릴 때가 있어요.
examples.en: Sometimes fear can paralyze a person.
The union tried to bring the subway to a halt with a strike.

explain: '마비시키다'는 몸의 감각이나 기능, 도시의 기능을 멈추게 할 때 써요. 원인이 되는 쪽이 주어예요. 치과에서 아픔을 없애는 주사는 보통 '마취'라고 해요. 결과를 말하면 '마비되다'를 쓰는데, '교통이 마비되다'가 뉴스에서 더 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: My leg became paralyzed because of the poison.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마비가 된 결과를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe the result of becoming paralyzed.

phrases.en: The hacking paralyzed the company's computer system.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기계나 도시의 기능을 멈추게 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for stopping the function of a machine or a city.

phrases.en: The cold numbed the feeling in my hands.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸의 감각이 없어지게 만드는 원인을 주어로 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The subject is the cause that makes bodily sensation disappear.

explain_en: 마비시키다 means to stop a body's sensation or function, or a city's functions. The cause is the subject. The shot a dentist gives to take away pain is usually called 마취 (anesthesia). For the result, Koreans use 마비되다, and '교통이 마비되다' (traffic is paralyzed) appears more often in the news.

examples.en: The child sits quietly and draws.
The puppy is waiting patiently.
You need to behave during class.

examples.ko: 동생은 손님이 오면 갑자기 얌전히 굴어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling suddenly behaves well when guests come.
The doctor told me to rest quietly at home.
She greeted politely and took her seat.

explain: 조용하고 점잖게 행동하는 모습에 써요. 아이나 동물에게 가장 많이 쓰고, '얌전히 있어'는 가만히 조용히 있으라고 할 때 써요. 어른에게 쓰면 '조용한 성격'이라는 칭찬이 될 수도 있고, 답답하다는 느낌도 줄 수 있어요.

phrases.en: Our puppy is very well-behaved.
phrases.nuance_ko: '얌전히'의 형용사 모양으로, 성격이나 모습을 설명해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adjective form, describing a quiet, gentle personality.

phrases.en: The child behaved quietly and got praised.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가만히 조용하게 있는 모습을 말할 때 가장 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common way to say someone stays calm and quiet.

phrases.example: 얌전한 아이가 갑자기 소리를 질러서 놀랐어요.
phrases.en: I was surprised when the quiet child suddenly shouted.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에 붙여 조용하고 점잖은 사람을 설명해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Placed before a noun to describe a quiet, well-mannered person.

explain_en: Sitting or behaving calmly and politely, often of children. Used for behaving in a quiet, well-mannered way, most often with children and animals. 얌전히 있어 means stay quiet and behave. For adults it can praise a calm personality, or hint that someone is too stiff.

examples.en: The factory polluted the river, and the fish died.
Car exhaust pollutes the city air.

examples.ko: 쓰레기를 함부로 버려서 바다를 오염시키면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not pollute the ocean by dumping trash carelessly.
I'm worried the oil will contaminate the ground.

examples.ko: 그 회사는 환경을 오염시킨 벌로 큰 벌금을 냈어요.
examples.en: The company paid a big fine for polluting the environment.

examples.ko: 손으로 직접 만지면 음식을 오염시킬 수 있어요.
examples.en: Touching food with your bare hands can contaminate it.

explain: 누군가나 무언가가 원인이 되어 더럽힐 때 써요. 당하는 쪽에서 말하면 '강물이 오염되다'가 돼요. '더럽히다'는 일상에서, 오염시키다는 환경 이야기에서 더 자주 써요.

phrases.en: Trash pollutes the environment.
phrases.nuance_ko: 환경 이야기에서 가장 자주 나오는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common collocation in talk about the environment.

phrases.en: We are careful not to pollute the river.
phrases.nuance_ko: '~지 않도록'과 같이 써서 조심하자는 뜻을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with '~지 않도록' to express being careful.

phrases.en: Oil made the sea dirty.
phrases.nuance_ko: '오염시키다'보다 일상적이고 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier, more everyday word than '오염시키다'.

explain_en: Use it when a person or thing is the cause of making something dirty. From the side of what gets dirty, you say '강물이 오염되다'. '더럽히다' is more common in daily life, and 오염시키다 more in talk about the environment.

examples.en: This product meets customers' needs.
I didn't meet the eligibility requirements, so I was rejected.
I want to satisfy my child's curiosity.

examples.ko: 조건을 모두 충족시키면 신청할 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you meet all the conditions, you can apply.

examples.ko: 새 가게는 다양한 입맛을 충족시키려고 메뉴를 늘렸어요.
examples.en: The new shop added menu items to satisfy different tastes.

examples.ko: 기준을 충족시키는 후보가 한 명도 없었어요.
examples.en: There was not a single candidate who met the criteria.

explain: 충족시키다는 요구, 조건, 기대, 호기심에 맞게 해 준다는 쪽이라 목적어에 '요구, 조건, 기준, 욕구'가 와요. 말할 때는 '맞추다'가 더 자주 쓰여요. 배고픔을 채우는 것은 '채우다'를 써요.

phrases.en: We try to meet our customers' expectations.
phrases.nuance_ko: '충족시키다'보다 말할 때 더 자주 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier word than 충족시키다 that is more common in speech.

phrases.example: 이 조건을 충족시키면 지원할 수 있어요.
phrases.en: If you meet this condition, you can apply.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조건, 기준, 자격과 함께 쓰는 대표적인 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A typical pairing with conditions, standards and qualifications.

phrases.en: I satisfy my curiosity by reading books.
phrases.nuance_ko: 호기심이나 욕구를 채워 줄 때도 자연스럽게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Also natural when satisfying curiosity or desires.

explain_en: 충족시키다 goes with objects like demand, condition, criterion and desire, meaning to satisfy them. In speech 맞추다 is used more often. For filling hunger, the word is 채우다.

examples.ko: 파도 때문에 해안의 침식이 심해지고 있어요.
examples.en: Coastal erosion is getting worse because of the waves.

examples.ko: 비가 많이 오면 산비탈의 침식이 빨라져요.
examples.en: When it rains a lot, erosion on the mountain slope speeds up.

examples.ko: 숲이 사라지자 토양 침식 문제가 생겼어요.
examples.en: After the forest disappeared, a soil erosion problem appeared.
This valley was formed by long-term erosion.
They planted trees on the shore to prevent erosion.

examples.ko: 강물에 의한 침식은 지리 시간에 배웠어요.
examples.en: We learned about erosion by river water in geography class.

explain: 지리나 환경 뉴스에서 '해안 침식', '토양 침식'처럼 자주 나와요. 짝말은 흙이 쌓이는 '퇴적'이에요. 글에서는 '신뢰의 침식'처럼 무언가가 조금씩 약해진다는 비유로도 써요.

phrases.en: The seaside cliff was eroded by the waves.
phrases.nuance_ko: '침식'을 동사처럼 써서 깎여 없어지는 과정을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb-like form for describing something being worn away.

phrases.en: We plant trees to prevent soil erosion.
phrases.nuance_ko: 환경 이야기에서 침식을 줄이거나 멈추려는 노력을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in environmental talk about reducing or stopping erosion.

phrases.example: 물의 침식 작용으로 깊은 계곡이 만들어졌어요.
phrases.en: A deep valley was formed by the erosion of water.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지리 수업에서 자연이 땅을 깎는 과정을 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in geography class for the natural process of wearing land away.

explain_en: In geography and environment news it often appears as '해안 침식' (coastal erosion) or '토양 침식' (soil erosion). Its paired word is '퇴적' (deposition), when soil piles up. In writing it is also used figuratively, as in '신뢰의 침식' (erosion of trust).

examples.en: Water is gushing out of the faucet.
It rained, so the stream is rushing along.
A pipe burst and water poured out.

examples.ko: 산속 샘에서 맑은 물이 콸콸 솟아요.
examples.en: Clear water gushes from the spring in the mountains.
Please don't leave the water running full blast.
I poured the water from the kettle into the cup in a rush.

explain: 많은 양의 물이 힘차게 쏟아지거나 흐르는 모습이에요. 적은 물이 가늘게 흐르면 '졸졸', 가늘게 계속 흐르면 '줄줄'이라고 해서 양과 세기가 달라요.

phrases.en: When I turned on the tap, water gushed out.
phrases.nuance_ko: 수도나 샤워기에서 물이 많이 나올 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when lots of water comes from a tap or shower.

phrases.en: The shower poured down heavily.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비나 물이 세게 한꺼번에 내릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when rain or water pours heavily all at once.

phrases.en: It's the rainy season, so the valley stream is rushing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 강이나 계곡물이 힘차게 흐르는 모습에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a river or stream flowing strongly.

explain_en: It shows a large amount of water pouring or flowing forcefully. A thin small flow is '졸졸', and a thin continuous flow is '줄줄', so the amount and strength differ.
